subject: docs/coop/artifacts/platform-tcb-contract.v1.json

blockers.title: The closed allowlist has neither an active-platform key nor a prequalification authorship boundary
evidence: Every permitted member is shaped only as {class, identity, versionOrDigest}. No field relates an entry to OS family, supported OS version/build, architecture, filesystem, or another qualified-platform profile; /platforms is a separate four-string list with no binding rule.

populatedTables reserves the concrete per-OS members as G22 qualification evidence but does not require a platform owner to author, sign, freeze, and review the active allowlist before the loader trace is collected. G22 is therefore not constrained to consume a pre-existing policy rather than infer or bless the dependencies observed on the qualification host.
The live G22 row quantifies over supported OS/filesystem/architecture, so a global union of entries is not an equivalent representation of its platform matrix.
blockers.impact: An entry intended for one platform can make the same name/version declared on every platform, and a qualification act can turn whatever the host happened to load into the allowlist it purports to test. The artifact therefore does not lock the claimed per-OS shape and cannot establish a closed allowlist without a later, unreviewed design decision.
blockers.requiredRepair: Define a platform-profile key and its exact relation to every TCB entry, including OS family, supported version/build selector, architecture, and filesystem where it affects resolution. If member population remains deferred, name its owning artifact and require the signed allowlist to be independently frozen before G22 execution; G22 must compare observations to that input and must never author it from the trace.

blockers.title: Name plus unconstrained version-or-digest is not a deterministic runtime-object identity rule
evidence: The declared tuple has an identity field, while sameMeans instead refers to an undefined declared name and then calls name plus version-or-digest the identity. The subject defines no name namespace, version grammar, exact-versus-range rule, tagged discriminator, digest algorithm/encoding, or rule selecting version versus digest by dependency class.

The explicit definition makes two different resolved objects with the same declared name and version identical even when their paths, bytes, build identities, architectures, or providers differ. Because version-only entries are permitted for every class, a digest need never close that substitution.

Certificate stores and font/ICU-class members may be collections, yet the contract gives them the same single opaque scalar without defining the collection boundary or how its runtime identity is measured.
blockers.impact: Identity drift and same-name substitution are adjudicator-dependent. A hostile object can preserve the declared label/version while changing the resolved bytes or collection contents and still be 'same' under the only rule the artifact states.
blockers.requiredRepair: Define class-appropriate, canonical identity evidence and comparison rules without choosing the concrete per-OS members: exact namespaces and selectors; normalized resolved-object or platform-authenticated build identity; digest algorithm where bytes/collections must be bound; collection membership/root rules; architecture/provider binding; and fail-closed handling for unknown or unobservable identity.

blockers.title: The claimed declared-versus-ambient split and alternate-search refusal predicate are absent
evidence: authorityClaim says the artifact locks a declared-vs-ambient split, but no field defines 'ambient'.

The subject necessarily permits declared host OS ABI/loader/libc/framework/certificate/font/ICU dependencies, while refuse lists ambient PATH / system-runtime / install-time substitution without stating that an actual host object matching the active platform entry is the narrow lawful TCB case or how that case takes precedence.

alternate loader search is named as a refusal and a test, but no permitted origin, loader identity, search root/order, environment-variable policy, or resolution route exists against which 'alternate' can be decided.
blockers.impact: One conforming reader can allow a matching host libc as declared TCB; another can reject it as system-runtime substitution; a third can accept a same-name object from an undeclared origin because origin is not part of identity. The central allow/refuse boundary is therefore non-deterministic.
blockers.requiredRepair: State one ordered runtime-resolution predicate: select the active qualified platform profile; observe the actual object and resolution route; allow only an exact entry match under the class-specific identity rule and declared origin/search policy; define every other source or route as ambient/alternate and refuse. Reconcile this narrow TCB exception explicitly with file 04's general no-system-runtime-substitution rule.

blockers.title: The retained trace and four test labels cannot prove full loader/system dependency closure
evidence: loaderTraces requires only that some loader trace be retained and makes absence a failure. It does not require the live row's full trace, define start/end and process-tree coverage, cover late/dynamic loads, bind events to the subject/allowlist/platform profile, or fail closed when an event cannot be identified.

Each negativeTests entry contains only {id, name}. There is no four-platform by OS/filesystem/architecture matrix, no per-class mutation set, no injected origin/search perturbation, and no exact expected refusal/diagnostic/evidence result.

The live G22 evidence text expressly includes negative undeclared libc/framework/cert/font/ICU/tool resolution and requires every declared platform to pass or be removed. A loader-only trace does not by itself establish system tool execution or certificate/font/data resolution, the subject names no companion process/file-resolution evidence, and it carries no all-platform pass/removal rule.
blockers.impact: A partial main-process trace plus one undeclared-library test can satisfy the artifact while a late load, child tool, certificate store, font, or ICU-class lookup enters from the ambient host. Retention is proven, but completeness and refusal are not.
blockers.requiredRepair: Define the complete observation boundary and evidence joins for the initial process, late loads, descendants/tools, and non-loader system-class accesses; require every event to match the signed active-profile table or fail. Define G22 test cases as the supported platform/filesystem/architecture cross-product with each required undeclared class, identity drift, and alternate-search mutation, including exact expected refusal and retained evidence; carry the pass-all-declared-platforms-or-remove-support rule.

shouldFix.title: The signed-closure TCB inventory has no named carrier or adjacent owner join
shouldFix.evidence: The subject requires a signed closure's TCB inventory but identifies no manifest/inventory field, artifact path, encoding owner, or dependency on the rows that own distribution inventory and signature binding. It also does not reserve that representation explicitly.
shouldFix.impact: A successor must either invent a new signed object under DR-126 or silently modify an adjacent schema, leaving the cross-row integration and signing boundary unreviewed.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Name the owning row/artifact and binding point for the TCB table, plus the dependency consequence if it is not yet available. Keep DR-126's identity policy here while explicitly leaving carrier encoding/signature ceremony with its adjacent owner.

measurements.evidence: Python hashlib(Path.read_bytes()) measured the subject at the expected 89913fd8a8f3c62cba4e18670a192de2ee5ed7033ec56982e491bf9b53831bbc; mode was 0444; strict duplicate-key-rejecting JSON parse passed.

measurements.check: Live source pins and verbatim custody
measurements.evidence: Live file 04 measured a74b4511... and its lines 161-166 equal all six carried strings byte-for-byte. Live file 08 measured 1cdcf9d4... and its unique DR-126 row at line 308 equals rowVerbatim byte-for-byte.

measurements.check: Recorded COORD snapshot and live cited decisions
measurements.evidence: The recorded 12d192f7... bytes reproduce exactly at repository commit 2327cf89106e3c58a317bf8b570697f3505dbbb8. The D-002 and D-006 entry segment hashes are respectively 8e19549a... and 9532e913... in both that snapshot and the live 39f372e1... file; later append-only movement did not change the cited platform or numeric-authority propositions.

measurements.check: D-002 platform and D-006 numeral discipline
measurements.evidence: platforms.slice1 is exactly macos/arm64, macos/x86_64, linux/x86_64, linux/arm64, matching D-002's four platforms, and Windows is expressly absent. None of D-006's 25/80 MB, startup, RSS, or 10% threshold numerals occurs in the subject.

The only declared member shape is {class, identity, versionOrDigest}; no member-to-platform profile relation exists, and populated member tables are called G22 evidence without a freeze-before-observe rule. See PTCB-V1-B1.
The explicit sameMeans rule compares only an unconstrained name and version-or-digest. No origin/search predicate or definition of ambient/alternate exists. See PTCB-V1-B2 and PTCB-V1-B3.

loaderTraces has only rule/preview prose; every negative test object has exactly id/name. No completeness boundary, evidence schema/join, per-class mutations, platform/filesystem matrix, or expected outcomes are present. See PTCB-V1-B4.

Immediately before completion, Python hashlib(Path.read_bytes()) remeasured the subject at 89913fd8a8f3c62cba4e18670a192de2ee5ed7033ec56982e491bf9b53831bbc with mode 0444. File 04 and file 08 retained their pinned a74b4511... and 1cdcf9d4... hashes. This reviewer wrote only its Codex reviewer artifact and made no commit.

attacks.attack: Populating per-OS package tables by fiat
attacks.evidence: No concrete package member is chosen, so literal population by fiat does not occur. However the contract neither defines a platform-keyed table shape nor requires the future table to be frozen before G22 observes the host; it miscasts an unbounded policy-authoring step as qualification evidence. See PTCB-V1-B1.

The artifact adds no archive, traversal, link, TOCTOU, descriptor, or spawn-binding rule and expressly leaves those to DR-G07/DR-103. Its unresolved alternate-loader versus loader-replacement boundary is handled as a DR-126 predicate defect in PTCB-V1-B3, not as extraction ownership.
No D-006 threshold numeral is present and the subject expressly leaves those values untouched.

attacks.attack: Ambient or undeclared system resolution is treated as lawful
attacks.evidence: The text does not positively authorize undeclared resolution, but its claimed declared-versus-ambient split is undefined. Same-name/version substitution and undeclared origins can be accepted under one reading, while all host-runtime resolution can be refused under another. See PTCB-V1-B2 and PTCB-V1-B3.

attacks.attack: SATISFIED, QUALIFIED, sealing, application, or implementation authorization
attacks.evidence: The subject is CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, binds NOTHING, recommends DO-NOT-SEAL, keeps DR-126 OPEN, calls G22 NAMED-NOT-AUTHORED, and expressly denies QUALIFIED/SATISFIED and docs/v2/implementation/ authority. This review grants none.

attacks.attack: Row-verbatim mismatch against live file 08 DR-126
attacks.evidence: The unique live row at line 308 is byte-for-byte identical to registerRowQuoted.rowVerbatim under the matching 1cdcf9d4... file hash.

verdictBasis: REJECT: 4 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX. ACCEPT requires 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX.
conclusion: REJECT at the frozen subject digest. The candidate preserves the live row and source quotation, does not populate packages or alter D-006, and grants no positive authority, but it does not define a platform-scoped predeclared allowlist, deterministic runtime identity, declared-versus-ambient/alternate-search predicate, or complete G22 observation and negative-test contract; its signed-inventory carrier is also unrouted.
coordinatorSummary: Issue a successor that keys a predeclared signed TCB table to an exact active platform profile; defines class-specific canonical identity and one fail-closed resolution predicate; specifies full process/tool/data observation plus the complete G22 mutation matrix; and names the adjacent signed-inventory carrier. Preserve the current DR-G07/D-006/platform/non-authority boundaries.
